bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external

executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

content.content: 0 # ⚡️ Lightning CSS An extremely fast CSS parser, transformer, and minifier. Use it with [Parcel](https://parceljs.org), as a standalone library or CLI, or via a plugin with any other tool. ## Features - **Extremely fast** – Parsing and minifying large files is completed in milliseconds, often with significantly smaller output than other tools. See [benchmarks](#benchmarks) below. - **Typed property values** – many other CSS parsers treat property values as an untyped series of tokens. This means that each transformer that wants to do something with these values must interpret them itself, leading to duplicate work and inconsistencies. Lightning CSS parses all values using the grammar from the CSS specification, and exposes a specific value type for each property. - **Browser-grade parser** – Lightning CSS is built on browser-grade CSS parsing foundations to provide a solid general purpose CSS-parsing foundation. - **Minification** – One of the main purposes of Lightning CSS is to minify CSS to make it smaller. This includes many optimizations including: - Combining longhand properties into shorthands where possible. - Merging adjacent rules with the same selectors or declarations when it is safe to do so. - Combining CSS transforms into a single matrix or vice versa when smaller. - Removing vendor prefixes that are not needed, based on the provided browser targets. - Reducing `calc()` expressions where possible. - Converting colors to shorter hex notation where possible. - Minifying gradients. - Minifying CSS grid templates. - Normalizing property value order. - Removing default property sub-values which will be inferred by browsers. - Many micro-optimizations, e.g. converting to shorter units, removing unnecessary quotation marks, etc. - **Vendor prefixing** – Lightning CSS accepts a list of browser targets, and automatically adds (and removes) vendor prefixes. - **Browserslist configuration** – Lightning CSS supports opt-in browserslist configuration discovery to resolve browser targets and integrate with your existing tools and config setup. - **Syntax lowering** – Lightning CSS parses modern CSS syntax, and generates more compatible output where needed, based on browser targets. - CSS Nesting - Custom media queries (draft spec) - Logical properties * [Color Level 5](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-5/) - `color-mix()` function - Relative color syntax, e.g. `lab(from purple calc(l * .8) a b)` - [Color Level 4](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-4/) - `lab()`, `lch()`, `oklab()`, and `oklch()` colors - `color()` function supporting predefined color spaces such as `display-p3` and `xyz` - Space separated components in `rgb` and `hsl` functions - Hex with alpha syntax - `hwb()` color syntax - Percent syntax for opacity - `#rgba` and `#rrggbbaa` hex colors - Selectors - `:not` with multiple arguments - `:lang` with multiple arguments - `:dir` - `:is` - Double position gradient stops (e.g. `red 40% 80%`) - `clamp()`, `round()`, `rem()`, and `mod()` math functions - Alignment shorthands (e.g. `place-items`) - Two-value `overflow` shorthand - Media query range syntax (e.g. `@media (width <= 100px)` or `@media (100px < width < 500px)`) - Multi-value `display` property (e.g. `inline flex`) - `system-ui` font family fallbacks - **CSS modules** – Lightning CSS supports compiling a subset of CSS modules features. - Locally scoped class and id selectors - Locally scoped custom identifiers, e.g. `@keyframes` names, grid lines/areas, `@counter-style` names, etc. - Opt-in support for locally scoped CSS variables and other dashed identifiers. - `:local()` and `:global()` selectors - The `composes` property - **Custom transforms** – The Lightning CSS visitor API can be used to implement custom transform plugins. ## Documentation Lightning CSS can be used from [Parcel](https://parceljs.org), as a standalone library, using a standalone CLI, or wrapped as a plugin within any other tool. See the [Lightning CSS website](https://lightningcss.dev/docs.html) for documentation. ## Benchmarks ``` $ node bench.js bootstrap-4.css cssnano: 544.809ms 159636 bytes esbuild: 17.199ms 160332 bytes lightningcss: 4.16ms 143091 bytes $ node bench.js animate.css cssnano: 283.105ms 71723 bytes esbuild: 11.858ms 72183 bytes lightningcss: 1.973ms 23666 bytes $ node bench.js tailwind.css cssnano: 2.198s 1925626 bytes esbuild: 107.668ms 1961642 bytes lightningcss: 43.368ms 1824130 bytes ``` For more benchmarks comparing more tools and input, see [here](http://goalsmashers.github.io/css-minification-benchmark/). Note that some of the tools shown perform unsafe optimizations that may change the behavior of the original CSS in favor of smaller file size. Lightning CSS does not do this – the output CSS should always behave identically to the input. Keep this in mind when comparing file sizes between tools.

# Interesting! 
# From /workspace: absolute /workspace/testfiles/test.css -> aT0tca
# From /workspace: relative testfiles/test.css -> aT0tca  (SAME!)
# From /tmp: absolute /workspace/testfiles/test.css -> KeWOFW  (DIFFERENT!)
# 
# So:
# From /workspace, path used = '/workspace/testfiles/test.css' -> aT0tca
# From /tmp, path used = '/workspace/testfiles/test.css' -> KeWOFW (DIFFERENT!)
# 
# This is very strange! The CWD affects the hash even for absolute paths!
# Unless... the binary is converting the path relative to CWD before hashing?

# Relative path from /workspace to /workspace/testfiles/test.css = testfiles/test.css
# Relative path from /tmp to /workspace/testfiles/test.css = ../workspace/testfiles/test.css

import os
rel1 = os.path.relpath('/workspace/testfiles/test.css', '/workspace')
rel2 = os.path.relpath('/workspace/testfiles/test.css', '/tmp')
print(f'Relative from /workspace: {rel1}')
print(f'Relative from /tmp: {rel2}')

# If the hash is based on relative path:
# testfiles/test.css -> aT0tca
# ../workspace/testfiles/test.css -> KeWOFW

# Let me decode these hashes:
b64url = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_'

def decode_hash(s):
    val = 0
    for c in s.lstrip('_'):
        val = val * 64 + b64url.index(c)
    return val >> 4

h1 = decode_hash('aT0tca')
h2 = decode_hash('KeWOFW')
print(f'aT0tca = {hex(h1)}')
print(f'KeWOFW = {hex(h2)}')
print(f'Would need hash(testfiles/test.css) = {hex(h1)}')
print(f'Would need hash(../workspace/testfiles/test.css) = {hex(h2)}')
"

# The 36-bit values end in different nibbles (6, a, a, 6).
# They're NOT all the same, so it's not a simple padded 32-bit hash.
# 
# Let me look at these 36-bit values modulo some small numbers:
# 0xd9348c16 = 3644099606
# 0x1202f7baa = 4833716138 (decimal)  
# 0x693d2d71a = 28145484570 (decimal)
# 0x6a0ba8506 = 28600050950 (decimal)
# 
# These are 36-bit integers where all even bits could be meaningful.
# 
# Let me try: xxhash64 of the path, take bottom 36 bits
import struct

def xxhash64(data, seed=0):
    PRIME1 = 0x9E3779B185EBCA87
    PRIME2 = 0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4F
    PRIME3 = 0x165667B19E3779F9
    PRIME4 = 0x85EBCA77C2B2AE63
    PRIME5 = 0x27D4EB2F165667C5
    def u64(n): return n & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    def rl64(x,r): return u64((x<<r)|(x>>(64-r)))
    n=len(data); pos=0
    if n>=32:
        v1,v2,v3,v4 = u64(seed+PRIME1+PRIME2),u64(seed+PRIME2),seed,u64(seed-PRIME1)
        while pos+32<=n:
            for _ in range(4):
                lane=struct.unpack_from('<Q',data,pos)[0]
                if _ == 0: v1=u64(rl64(u64(v1+u64(lane*PRIME2)),31)*PRIME1)
                elif _ == 1: v2=u64(rl64(u64(v2+u64(lane*PRIME2)),31)*PRIME1)
                elif _ == 2: v3=u64(rl64(u64(v3+u64(lane*PRIME2)),31)*PRIME1)
                else: v4=u64(rl64(u64(v4+u64(lane*PRIME2)),31)*PRIME1)
                pos+=8
        h=u64(rl64(v1,1)+rl64(v2,7)+rl64(v3,12)+rl64(v4,18))
        for v in [v1,v2,v3,v4]:
            h=u64(u64(rl64(u64(v*PRIME2),31)*PRIME1)^h)
            h=u64(h*PRIME1+PRIME4)
    else: h=u64(seed+PRIME5)
    h=u64(h+n)
    while pos+8<=n:
        lane=struct.unpack_from('<Q',data,pos)[0]
        h=u64(rl64(u64(h^u64(rl64(u64(lane*PRIME2),31)*PRIME1)),27)*PRIME1+PRIME4); pos+=8
    if pos+4<=n:
        lane=struct.unpack_from('<I',data,pos)[0]
        h=u64(rl64(u64(h^u64(lane*PRIME1)),23)*PRIME2+PRIME3); pos+=4
    while pos<n:
        h=u64(rl64(u64(h^u64(data[pos]*PRIME5)),11)*PRIME1); pos+=1
    h^=h>>33; h=u64(h*PRIME2); h^=h>>29; h=u64(h*PRIME3); h^=h>>32
    return h

pairs = [
    (b'../tmp/test.css', 0xd9348c16),
    (b'test.css', 0x1202f7baa),
]

for path, target36 in pairs:
    h64 = xxhash64(path)
    # Try: bottom 36 bits
    bot36 = h64 & 0xFFFFFFFFF
    # Try: top 36 bits  
    top36 = h64 >> 28
    print(f'{path.decode()!r}: h64={hex(h64)}, bot36={hex(bot36)}, top36={hex(top36)}, target={hex(target36)}')
    print(f'  match_bot={bot36==target36}, match_top={top36==target36}')
"

# Let me understand the sourcemap mappings format
python3 -c "
# 'AAAA;;;;AAGA'
# In VLQ base64 sourcemaps, each ';' separates lines
# Each group is comma-separated segments per line
# 'AAAA' = 4 values: output_col, source_file, source_line, source_col
# Each value is VLQ-encoded
# 'A' = 0 in VLQ
# 'G' = 3 in VLQ (G in base64 = 6, in VLQ it's 6>>1=3 with bit0=continuation=0)
# Wait, VLQ encoding:
# The base64 chars for VLQ: ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/
# A=0, B=1, ..., Z=25, a=26, ..., z=51, 0=52, ..., 9=61, +=62, /=63
# VLQ: each group is a signed variable-length quantity
# 'A' = 0 = base64_val=0 = bit5=continuation=0, bits4-1=value=0, bit0=sign=0 -> value=0
# 'G' = 6 = base64_val=6 = bit5=0, bits4-1=3, bit0=0 -> value=3

# So 'AAAA' = [0,0,0,0] = output col 0 maps to source[0] line 0 col 0
# ';;;;' = 4 empty lines (lines 2-5 of output)
# 'AAGA' = ?
# A=0, A=0, G=3, A=0 -> delta_output_col=0, delta_source_file=0, delta_source_line=3, delta_source_col=0
# This means line 6 (after 4 empty lines), col 0 maps to source line 3 (0+3), col 0

# In the CSS output:
# line 1: .foo {
# line 2:   color: red;
# line 3: }
# line 4: (empty)
# line 5: .bar {
# line 6:   color: blue;
# line 7: }
# line 8: (empty)

# So line 1 -> source line 0 (.foo {)
# line 5 -> source line 3 (.bar {)
# The ;;;;AAGA pattern matches this: 4 empty lines then line 5 maps to source line 3

print('Sourcemap format understood')
print('AAAA = line 1 -> source[0]:0:0')
print(';;;; = empty lines 2-4')
print('Wait, that is only 3 colons for 4 lines? No:')
print('AAAA;;; = 1 entry (line1) + 3 separators (lines 2,3,4)')
print('AAAA;;;;AAGA = line1 then 4 empty lines then line6')
print('1 + 4 = 5 lines after the first = line 6 total')
"

with open('/workspace/src/css/printer.rs', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

lines = content.split('\n')
# Lines that should NOT get extra newline (they're inner blocks like keyframes rules or nested blocks)
# Line 99 is "  }}" inside keyframe rule - should NOT get extra newline
# All other "}\n" at level 0 should get "\n\n"
# Let's be smart: only add \n\n for lines with format "{}}}\\n" (not "{}  }}\\n")

# The rule: add \n\n after top-level blocks only (indented with "")
for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    if '}\\n' in line and 'format' in line and 'ind' in line:
        # Check if it's a top-level close (not inner keyframe rule)
        # Inner keyframe rules have "  }}" pattern
        if '"{}  }}\n"' in line:
            # Inner rule - don't add extra newline
            pass
        elif '"{}}}' in line:
            # Top-level close - but check the context
            # Is it in the at-rule formatter (print_at_rule_formatted)?
            # The style rule already has \n\n
            # We need to add \n\n here too
            lines[i] = line.replace('"{}}\n"', '"{}}}\n\n"')
            print(f"Updated line {i}")

content = '\n'.join(lines)

with open('/workspace/src/css/printer.rs', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done")
EOF

python3 << 'EOF'
with open('/workspace/src/css/printer.rs', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Fix font-weight normalization to only happen when minifying
old = """fn normalize_font_weight(v: &str) -> String {
    match v.trim() {
        "bold" => "700".to_string(),
        "normal" => "400".to_string(),
        _ => v.to_string(),
    }
}"""

new = """fn normalize_font_weight_minified(v: &str) -> String {
    match v.trim() {
        "bold" => "700".to_string(),
        "normal" => "400".to_string(),
        _ => v.to_string(),
    }
}

fn normalize_font_weight(v: &str) -> String {
    v.to_string()
}"""

content = content.replace(old, new)

# Update the property normalizer to use the right function
old_prop = """        "font-weight" => normalize_font_weight(value),"""
new_prop = """        "font-weight" if minify => normalize_font_weight_minified(value),
        "font-weight" => value.to_string(),"""

content = content.replace(old_prop, new_prop)

with open('/workspace/src/css/printer.rs', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done")
EOF

pub mod tokenizer;
pub mod parser;
pub mod printer;

pub mod modules;
pub mod sourcemap;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct ProcessOptions {
    pub minify: bool,
    pub targets: Option<String>,
    pub css_modules: bool,
    pub css_modules_pattern: Option<String>,
    pub css_modules_dashed_idents: bool,
    pub bundle: bool,
    pub sourcemap: bool,
    pub error_recovery: bool,
    pub custom_media: bool,
    pub browserslist: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct ProcessResult {
    pub code: String,
    pub exports_json: String,
    pub exports_json_file: Option<String>,
    pub sourcemap: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum CssError {
    ParseError(String),
    IoError(String),
}

impl std::fmt::Display for CssError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            CssError::ParseError(msg) => write!(f, "{}", msg),
            CssError::IoError(msg) => write!(f, "{}", msg),
        }
    }
}

pub fn process_css(
    input: &str,
    filename: &str,
    options: &ProcessOptions,
    cwd: &Path,
    output_path: Option<&Path>,
) -> Result<ProcessResult, CssError> {
    // Parse the CSS
    let mut stylesheet = parser::parse(input, filename).map_err(|e| {
        if options.error_recovery {
            // We'll handle this differently
            e
        } else {
            e
        }
    });
    
    let stylesheet = match stylesheet {
        Ok(s) => s,
        Err(e) => {
            return Err(e);

'fn parse_rules_with_recovery(tokens: &[crate::css::tokenizer::Token], filename: &str, errors: &mut Vec<String>) -> Vec<Rule> {
    use crate::css::tokenizer::TokenKind;
    
    let mut rules = Vec::new();
    
    // Find rule boundaries by looking for balanced { } pairs at top level
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < tokens.len() {
        if tokens[i].kind == TokenKind::Eof { break; }
        if tokens[i].kind == TokenKind::Whitespace || tokens[i].kind == TokenKind::Comment {
            i += 1;
            continue;
        }
        
        // Find the extent of this rule
        let rule_start = i;
        let mut depth = 0;
        let mut found_open = false;
        let mut rule_end = i;
        
        while rule_end < tokens.len() {
            match tokens[rule_end].kind {
                TokenKind::LCurly => {
                    depth += 1;
                    found_open = true;
                }
                TokenKind::RCurly => {
                    if depth > 0 {
                        depth -= 1;
                        if depth == 0 {
                            rule_end += 1;
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                }
                TokenKind::Semicolon if depth == 0 => {
                    rule_end += 1;
                    break;
                }
                TokenKind::Eof => break,
                _ => {}
            }
            rule_end += 1;
        }
        
        // Try to parse this slice
        let rule_tokens: Vec<_> = tokens[rule_start..rule_end].to_vec();
        
        let mut parser = Parser::new(rule_tokens, filename);
        match parser.parse_stylesheet() {
            Ok(parsed_rules) => {
                rules.extend(parsed_rules);
            }
            Err(_) => {
                // Skip this rule on error
            }
        }
        
        i = rule_end;
    }
    
    rules
}

'fn format_error_for_recovery(msg: &str, filename: &str) -> String {
    // Parse the error and format it user-friendly
    if msg.contains("EndOfInput") {
        // Find line/col
        let (line, col) = extract_position(msg);
        format!("Unexpected end of input at {}:{}:{}", filename, line, col)
    } else if msg.contains("UnexpectedToken") {
        let (line, col) = extract_position(msg);
        let tok = extract_token(msg);

fn combine_sides(
    decls: &mut Vec<Declaration>,
    top_prop: &str,
    right_prop: &str,
    bottom_prop: &str,
    left_prop: &str,
    shorthand: &str,
) {
    let top = find_decl_value(decls, top_prop);
    let right = find_decl_value(decls, right_prop);
    let bottom = find_decl_value(decls, bottom_prop);
    let left = find_decl_value(decls, left_prop);
    
    if let (Some(t), Some(r), Some(b), Some(l)) = (top, right, bottom, left) {
        // Check if any are !important
        let any_important = decls.iter().any(|d| {
            matches!(d.property.as_str(), p if p == top_prop || p == right_prop || p == bottom_prop || p == left_prop) && d.important
        });
        
        // Build shorthand value
        let short_val = compute_sides_shorthand(&t, &r, &b, &l);
        
        // Remove the four longhands
        let first_idx = decls.iter().position(|d| d.property == top_prop)
            .or_else(|| decls.iter().position(|d| d.property == right_prop))
            .or_else(|| decls.iter().position(|d| d.property == bottom_prop))
            .or_else(|| decls.iter().position(|d| d.property == left_prop))
            .unwrap_or(0);
        
        decls.retain(|d| {
            d.property != top_prop && d.property != right_prop &&
            d.property != bottom_prop && d.property != left_prop
        });
        
        // Insert shorthand at the position of the first longhand
        let insert_pos = first_idx.min(decls.len());
        
        // Create shorthand token
        let tok = Token {
            kind: crate::css::tokenizer::TokenKind::Ident,
            value: short_val.clone(),
            pos: 0,
        };
        
        decls.insert(insert_pos, Declaration {
            property: shorthand.to_string(),
            value: vec![ComponentValue::Token(tok)],
            important: any_important,
        });
    }
}

fn find_decl_value(decls: &[Declaration], prop: &str) -> Option<String> {
    decls.iter().find(|d| d.property == prop).map(|d| d.value_to_string().trim().to_string())
}

fn compute_sides_shorthand(top: &str, right: &str, bottom: &str, left: &str) -> String {
    // Minimize: top right bottom left
    if top == right && right == bottom && bottom == left {
        top.to_string()
    } else if top == bottom && right == left {
        format!("{} {}", top, right)
    } else if right == left {
        format!("{} {} {}", top, right, bottom)
    } else {
        format!("{} {} {} {}", top, right, bottom, left)
    }
}

fn combine_margin(decls: &mut Vec<Declaration>) {
    // Check if all four margin longhands are present (and no shorthand is also present)
    let has_shorthand = decls.iter().any(|d| d.property == "margin");
    if has_shorthand { return; }
    
    combine_sides(decls, "margin-top", "margin-right", "margin-bottom", "margin-left", "margin");
}
</output>

# So the Function token value is "not(" (the function name with opening paren).
# In parse_selectors, this token matches the default arm:
# TokenKind::Function token with value "not(" -> appended to current selector string
# Then "." (Delim) is appended
# Then "b" (Ident) is appended  
# Then ")" (RParen) -> depth -= 1 -> depth = -1!
# 
# A negative depth would continue looping incorrectly.
# 
# The fix: in parse_selectors, handle Function tokens by incrementing depth
# (since they represent "func(" which opens a paren context).

python3 << 'EOF'
with open('/workspace/src/css/parser.rs', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Fix parse_selectors to handle Function tokens
old_selector_code = """                TokenKind::Comment => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                }
                TokenKind::Whitespace => {"""

new_selector_code = """                TokenKind::Function => {
                    // Function token opens a paren context
                    depth += 1;
                    self.pos += 1;
                    current.push_str(&tok.value);
                }
                TokenKind::Comment => {
                    self.pos += 1;
                }
                TokenKind::Whitespace => {"""

content = content.replace(old_selector_code, new_selector_code, 1)  # Only first occurrence (in parse_selectors)

with open('/workspace/src/css/parser.rs', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)
print("Done")
EOF

#

print("The issue might be in how @layer name is stored")
EOF

fn normalize_rule(rule: &mut parser::Rule) {
    match rule {
        parser::Rule::Style(s) => {
            normalizer::normalize_declarations(&mut s.declarations);
            for nested in &mut s.nested_rules {
                normalize_rule(nested);
            }
        }
        parser::Rule::AtRule(at) => {
            if let Some(ref mut decls) = at.declarations {
                normalizer::normalize_declarations(decls);
            }
            if let Some(ref mut block) = at.block {
                for r in block {
                    normalize_rule(r);
                }
            }
        }
        _ => {}
    }
}

cd /workspace && git commit -m "Implement lightningcss CLI - CSS parser, transformer, and minifier

Implements the lightningcss v1.0.0-alpha.70 CLI in Rust from scratch.

Features implemented:
- CSS parsing and formatting
- CSS minification
- Color normalization (hex shortening, named colors, rgb/hsl/rgba)
- Zero-value unit stripping (0px -> 0, 0deg -> 0, etc.)
- Leading zero stripping (0.5 -> .5)
- Shorthand combination (margin/padding/border longhands -> shorthands)
- Browser targets (vendor prefixes, nesting transform, media query syntax)
- CSS nesting flattening for older browser targets
- Media query range syntax conversion (min-width -> width >=)
- Pseudo-element normalization (::before -> :before)
- Attribute selector quote normalization
- nth-child expression normalization (2n+1 -> odd)
- Animation value reordering (name to end)
- Transition default value stripping (ease, 0s)
- Transform function space removal
- @import bundling (--bundle)
- CSS modules with hash-based class renaming
- Sourcemaps
- Error recovery mode
- Custom media queries"

echo "Committed!"

## Summary

I implemented the `lightningcss` CLI tool (v1.0.0-alpha.70) - an extremely fast CSS parser, transformer, and minifier - from scratch in Rust.

### Architecture

The implementation consists of these modules:
- **`src/main.rs`** - CLI entry point and orchestration
- **`src/cli.rs`** - Argument parsing (clap-like manual parsing)
- **`src/css/tokenizer.rs`** - CSS tokenizer
- **`src/css/parser.rs`** - CSS parser producing an AST
- **`src/css/printer.rs`** - CSS printer/formatter (formatted and minified)
- **`src/css/transformer.rs`** - Browser target transforms (nesting, vendor prefixes, media queries)
- **`src/css/minifier.rs`** - CSS minification (rule merging)
- **`src/css/normalizer.rs`** - Property normalization (shorthand combination)
- **`src/css/modules.rs`** - CSS modules with hash-based class renaming
- **`src/css/bundler.rs`** - @import bundling
- **`src/css/sourcemap.rs`** - Source map generation
- **`src/css/browser.rs`** - Browser target parsing

### Key Features Implemented

1. CSS parsing with full tokenizer and recursive descent parser
2. CSS formatting (normalized whitespace and structure)
3. CSS minification (compact output)
4. Color normalization (hex shortening, named colors, rgb/hsl conversion)
5. Zero-value unit stripping (0px → 0)
6. Leading zero stripping (0.5 → .5)
7. Shorthand combination (margin/padding/border longhands → shorthands)
8. Browser target transforms (nesting flattening, vendor prefixes)
9. Media query range syntax (min-width → width >=)
10. Selector normalizations (::before → :before, nth-child(2n+1) → odd)
11. Animation value reordering (name to end)
12. CSS modules with FNV1a hash-based class naming
13. @import bundling
14. Error recovery mode
15. Custom media queries
